title: The actual scalar tensor, its unit-normalized derived pair, and its adjuncts
statement: Let E and Omega be normed fields in the same universe with an E-algebra structure on Omega and a continuous inclusion h. Write A=C(-,E) and B=C(-,Omega) for the all-continuous internal rings [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], and use their internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Ordinary tensor is the existing extension-of-scalars coequalizer along the continuous coefficient map. Its pure section z tensor x is z times the actual ordinary unit applied to x. When scalar restriction is exact, a DerivedTensor consists of a total left derived functor T, its canonical comparison Qh T -> tensor Qh, its universal property, and an adjunction to exact derived restriction whose unit followed by restricted comparison and exact-functor transport equals Qh of the ordinary scalar unit on every homotopy object. For normalized Koszul realizations [lem-sfb-tame-inertia-continuous-koszul], tensorMap is the ordinary adjunct of the literal coefficient inclusion, and mate is the derived adjunct of the actual representation coefficient map. These are precisely the definitions previously bundled with the scalar-mate theorem, with the same data, fields and equations.
